headline: AMD chief executive Lisa Su has said she expects AI computing to shift towards running models for users and the market for data-centre AI chips to reach about $1.5 trillion by 2030.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a company forecast at a trade event with no independent check.
importance_line: A chip maker's own forecast of a $1.5 trillion market shows how large the data-centre build-out might become, which matters first to the communities and power systems around those sites, then to chip buyers and investors, but it is AMD's projection, made at a trade event, with no independent estimate in the report.
summary: StockTwits reports that Lisa Su, chief executive of the US chip maker AMD (Advanced Micro Devices), told the 2026 OCP Global Summit that this is "the year of inference", the running of trained AI models for users, which AMD believes is now about 60% of the AI market, and that the market for data-centre AI chips should approach $1.5 trillion by 2030. She also said AMD's Helios rack system, which links 72 chips, began production shipments in September to customers including Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle and Anthropic, and that AMD expects demand for server processors to grow about 50% a year to more than $200 billion by 2030; all of these are AMD's own forecasts.
notes: Read from fulltext (StockTwits article carried by Yahoo Finance; the Yahoo link is the page read). The date of the talk is not stated.
